title: Introduction to the particulate nature of matter; The nuclear atom

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Condensation
items.clue: The change from gas to liquid, e.g. H₂O(g) → H₂O(l); energy is released.

items.label: Filtration
items.clue: Separation of an insoluble solid from a liquid (or from a solution) by passing the mixture through a filter such as filter paper.

items.label: Heterogeneous mixture
items.clue: A mixture whose composition is not uniform throughout: it contains two or more phases, and the components can often be seen separately.

items.label: Homogeneous mixture
items.clue: A mixture with a uniform composition throughout, in a single phase, so that the components cannot be seen separately and every sample taken from it has the same composition.

questions.stem: A substance at room temperature has a fixed volume but takes the shape of its container. Which statement about its particles is correct?

options.text: They are close together but not in fixed positions
They are spaced about halfway between those of a solid and a gas
The spaces between the particles are filled with air
Each one is soft, so it changes shape as the substance flows

questions.explanation: This is a liquid. Its particles are close together, as in a solid (liquids are barely compressible), but not held in fixed positions, so they move past one another and the liquid takes the shape of its container.

questions.stem: A molecular solid, X, is heated at a constant rate. Its temperature rises to 80 °C, stays at 80 °C for six minutes while the solid melts, and then rises again. Which explains why the temperature stays constant while X melts?

options.text: The energy supplied is lost to the surroundings, so X absorbs none of it as it melts
The energy absorbed overcomes attractions between molecules; their average Ek is constant
The energy absorbed breaks the covalent bonds within each of the molecules of X
The energy absorbed is used to make each molecule expand as the solid melts

questions.stem: Which statement about the nucleus of an atom is correct?

options.text: It takes up most of the atom's volume, with electrons at its surface.
Its density is far greater than the average density of the atom.
It contains only about two-thirds of the mass of the atom.
It contains the electrons as well as the protons and neutrons.

questions.explanation: Correct. Nearly all of the atom's mass is in the nucleus, because electrons are so light. The nucleus is of order 10⁻¹⁵ m across and the atom of order 10⁻¹⁰ m, so the nucleus occupies only about (10⁻¹⁵ ÷ 10⁻¹⁰)³ = 10⁻¹⁵ of the atom's volume. Nearly all the mass in a tiny volume makes the nucleus extremely dense.

questions.stem: Two atoms have the same atomic number but different mass numbers. Which statement about these atoms is correct?

options.text: They belong to different elements, as they contain different numbers of nucleons in total.
They belong to the same element, as they differ only in their numbers of neutrons.
They have different numbers of electrons, as their mass numbers are different.
They undergo different chemical reactions, because their atoms have different masses.

questions.explanation: Correct. The atomic number (number of protons) defines the element. Different mass numbers with the same atomic number mean different numbers of neutrons: the atoms are isotopes of one element.

questions.stem: Which statement about the vaporization of water is correct?

options.text: Evaporation can take place only once the water has reached its boiling point
Evaporation takes place at the surface, even well below the boiling point
The large bubbles in boiling water contain hydrogen and oxygen
The large bubbles in boiling water are air from the gaps between the particles

questions.explanation: Water particles have a range of kinetic energies. At any temperature some particles at the surface have enough energy to overcome the attractions and escape, which is why puddles dry at 20 °C. Boiling, with bubbles of vapour throughout the liquid, happens at the boiling point.

questions.stem: A sample of neon gas is at 77 °C. It is heated until the average kinetic energy of its atoms has doubled. What is its new temperature? (T/K = T/°C + 273)
questions.explanation: Average kinetic energy is proportional to temperature in kelvin. 77 °C = 350 K; doubling gives 700 K; 700 − 273 = 427 °C.

questions.stem: Which statement about the relative masses and relative charges of subatomic particles is correct?

options.text: A proton carries a larger charge than an electron does.
A neutron carries a charge opposite in sign to a proton's.
A proton and an electron carry charges that are equal in size.
An electron has a mass close to that of a proton.

questions.explanation: Correct. Relative charges: proton +1, electron −1, equal in size and opposite in sign. This is why a neutral atom has equal numbers of protons and electrons. (Their masses are very different: proton 1, electron about 0.0005.)

questions.stem: Chlorine (atomic number 17) has isotopes with mass numbers 35 and 37. Pure samples of ³⁵Cl₂ gas and ³⁷Cl₂ gas are compared at the same temperature and pressure. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The ³⁷Cl₂ gas diffuses more slowly than ³⁵Cl₂.
The two gases diffuse at the same rate as each other.
The two gases undergo different chemical reactions.
The ³⁷Cl₂ molecules contain more electrons than ³⁵Cl₂.

questions.explanation: Correct. At the same temperature the molecules of both gases have the same mean kinetic energy, so the heavier ³⁷Cl₂ molecules move more slowly on average and the gas diffuses more slowly. Rate of diffusion is a physical property that differs between isotopes.

questions.stem: Which change of state is correctly named and correctly represented by an equation with state symbols?

options.text: Melting: NaCl(s) → NaCl(aq)
Condensation: H₂O(g) → H₂O(s)
Boiling: H₂O(aq) → H₂O(g)
Sublimation: CO₂(s) → CO₂(g)

questions.explanation: At atmospheric pressure solid carbon dioxide ('dry ice') changes directly into gas without becoming liquid. A direct change from solid to gas is sublimation, and the state symbols (s) and (g) show exactly that.

questions.stem: Which statement about temperature is correct?

options.text: A temperature of 0 K is the same as a temperature of 273 °C
Doubling a temperature in °C doubles the average kinetic energy
A rise of 1 K is exactly the same size as a rise of 1 °C
Temperature in K measures how much heat a sample holds

questions.explanation: The kelvin has the same incremental value as the Celsius degree; the two scales differ only in their zero (0 K = −273 °C). So a temperature change of 25 °C is a change of 25 K.

questions.stem: An atom of sodium, ²³₁₁Na (mass number 23, atomic number 11), forms the ion Na⁺. How does the mass of the ion compare with the mass of the atom?

options.text: It is smaller by a negligible amount, because one electron was lost.
It is larger by a negligible amount, because one electron has been gained.
It is larger by about one unit, because the ion has gained one proton.
It is smaller by about one unit, because the ion has lost one electron.

questions.explanation: Correct. A 1+ ion has one electron fewer than its atom; the numbers of protons and neutrons do not change. An electron's relative mass is about 0.0005, so the loss is negligible (about 0.002% of the mass of the atom).

questions.stem: A sample of chlorine contains 75.8% chlorine-35 (relative isotopic mass 34.97) and 24.2% chlorine-37 (relative isotopic mass 36.97). What is the relative atomic mass of chlorine in this sample?
questions.explanation: Correct. A_r = (75.8 × 34.97 + 24.2 × 36.97) ÷ 100 = (2650.7 + 894.7) ÷ 100 = 35.45. It lies closer to 34.97 because chlorine-35 is the more abundant isotope.

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of element E shows three peaks from singly charged atomic ions: m/z 24 (relative abundance 100), m/z 25 (relative abundance 12.7) and m/z 26 (relative abundance 13.9). What is the relative atomic mass of E, calculated from these data?

The mass spectrum of element X, showing only the peaks from singly charged atomic ions (X⁺), has two peaks: m/z 79 (relative abundance 100) and m/z 81 (relative abundance 97.3). Atomic numbers: selenium 34, bromine 35, gadolinium 64, gold 79. Which element is X?

options.text: Element X is selenium (A_r 78.97).
Element X is gold (A_r 196.97).
Element X is bromine (A_r 79.90).
Element X is gadolinium (A_r 157.25).

questions.explanation: Correct. A_r = (79 × 100 + 81 × 97.3) ÷ (100 + 97.3) = 15 781.3 ÷ 197.3 = 79.99, which matches bromine (79.90) and no other option. The two peaks are two isotopes of nearly equal abundance.

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of a sample of copper shows two peaks from singly charged atomic ions: m/z 63 (relative abundance 100) and m/z 65 (relative abundance 44.6). What do these peaks show?

options.text: The sample also contains a second element, of mass 65.
The A_r of copper is 63, which is the m/z of the tallest peak.
The A_r of copper is 64, the mean of the two m/z values.
Copper atoms exist with two numbers of neutrons, 34 and 36.

questions.explanation: Correct. Each peak from singly charged atomic ions corresponds to one isotope. Copper atoms all have the same number of protons, so masses of 63 and 65 mean two different numbers of neutrons (34 and 36).
